D1:
Why: Core is the LOWEST AnimationPriority (Action4 > Action3 > Action2 > Action > Movement > Idle > Core). The default Animate script plays idle/walk at Idle/Movement, which outranks your Core swing on every joint they both key, so the arms follow idle/walk. (Don't compare Priority.Value; Core = 1000 breaks numeric ordering.) Also Humanoid:LoadAnimation is deprecated, and loading a new track on every click leaks tracks.
Fix: re-export the clip at Action (or set the track priority before Play), load once via the Animator, and cache the track:
```lua
local char = player.Character or player.CharacterAdded:Wait()
local animator = char:WaitForChild("Humanoid"):WaitForChild("Animator")
local track = animator:LoadAnimation(script.SwingAnim)
track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action -- Action2-4 for overlays
tool.Activated:Connect(function()
    track:Play()
end)
```
Only joints the clip keys are overridden, so an upper-body swing lets legs keep walking. Reload the track on CharacterAdded.

-- when done:

D4:
Problems:
1) 5000 is less than the platform's weight. Lift needs Force.Y > AssemblyMass * workspace.Gravity (196.2 studs/s^2). A 20x2x20 plastic part (density 0.7) is 800 stud^3, mass ~560, weight ~110,000.
2) Force is applied at the corner attachment (ApplyAtCenterOfMass = false), producing torque, so it tilts.
3) RelativeTo defaults to Attachment0, so the force rotates with the part: once tilted, 'up' points sideways and it slides and spins away.
Correct setup:
```lua
local att = Instance.new("Attachment", platform) -- at center
local vf = Instance.new("VectorForce")
vf.Attachment0 = att
vf.ApplyAtCenterOfMass = true
vf.RelativeTo = Enum.ActuatorRelativeTo.World
vf.Force = Vector3.new(0, platform.AssemblyMass * workspace.Gravity, 0) -- exact hover; add extra to rise
vf.Parent = platform
```
Add AlignOrientation (PrimaryAxisParallel to world up) to keep it level, and for controlled height/speed use AlignPosition or LinearVelocity; a constant net force accelerates forever. Recompute if mass changes; anchored parts ignore it.
D5:
Leaks:
1) sessions[player] is never removed, so each player's table (and history, which grows) and the Player reference stay forever.
2) Every CharacterAdded creates a new Heartbeat connection that is never disconnected. RunService.Heartbeat is long-lived, so destroying the character does not disconnect it; respawns stack connections that keep running updateAura on dead characters and pin them in memory.
3) history grows unbounded.
Fix:
```lua
local sessions = {}
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    local s = { kills = 0, history = {}, conns = {} }
    sessions[player] = s
    player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(char)
        if s.aura then s.aura:Disconnect() end
        s.aura = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function() updateAura(char) end)
        char.Destroying:Once(function()
            if s.aura then s.aura:Disconnect(); s.aura = nil end
        end)
    end)
end)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
    local s = sessions[player]
    if s and s.aura then s.aura:Disconnect() end
    sessions[player] = nil
end)
```
Cap history (ring buffer). Better: one shared Heartbeat loop iterating active auras rather than one connection per character.

```lua
local PathfindingService = game:GetService("PathfindingService")
local path = PathfindingService:CreatePath({
    AgentRadius = 2, AgentHeight = 5, AgentCanJump = true,
    Costs = { Lava = math.huge, Water = 20 },
})
local function moveTo(humanoid: Humanoid, target: Vector3)
    local root = humanoid.Parent.HumanoidRootPart
    local ok = pcall(path.ComputeAsync, path, root.Position, target)
    if not ok or path.Status ~= Enum.PathStatus.Success then return false end
    for _, wp in path:GetWaypoints() do
        if wp.Action == Enum.PathWaypointAction.Jump then humanoid.Jump = true end
        humanoid:MoveTo(wp.Position)
        local reached = false
        local c = humanoid.MoveToFinished:Once(function(r) reached = r end)
        local t = os.clock()
        while not reached and os.clock() - t < 2.5 do task.wait() end
        c:Disconnect()
        if not reached then return moveTo(humanoid, target) end -- recompute
    end
    return true
end
```
Rules: Costs keys are material names or PathfindingModifier/PathfindingLink Labels; default 1; math.huge = never traversable. Lava zones: a PathfindingModifier with Label "Lava" in an anchored, CanCollide=false volume part. Water: finite high cost so it is only used if no dry route. Waypoint Action Jump -> humanoid.Jump. ComputeAsync yields/errors: pcall + check Status. MoveToFinished can hang: per-waypoint timeout. Handle path.Blocked (recompute if blocked index >= current). Network owner nil for NPC root; one Path per agent size.

D11:
Cars: give the driver network ownership. On VehicleSeat.Occupant changed, call seat:SetNetworkOwner(driverPlayer) (whole assembly); on exit, SetNetworkOwner(nil) (or back to auto). The driver simulates locally, so no input-to-server round-trip lag. Unanchored, CanSetNetworkOwnership() true.
NPC guards: server-owned. After spawning, root:SetNetworkOwner(nil) so automatic ownership never hands them to a nearby player. Otherwise an exploiter who owns a guard can fling/teleport it.
Security: the network owner is authoritative for that assembly's physics. A driver can teleport the car, speed-hack, set absurd/NaN velocities to fling others, or spoof Touched. So: server sanity-checks owned vehicles (displacement/speed per tick vs max with strikes, NaN checks, server-granted allowances for boosts), validates gameplay with server distance checks, never awards from client-owned Touched alone, resets/ejects on violations. Avoid frequent ownership switching (jitter). Server-owned guards' collisions with client-owned cars can still push them, so clamp guard velocity and keep damage logic server-side.

What the engine keeps: standard DataStores version every write; one backup version per key per UTC hour is retained, each kept 30 days after being superseded. (Ordered DataStores have no versions.)
Tool (server, e.g. admin command or Studio/Open Cloud):
```lua
local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("PlayerData")
local key = "Player_" .. userId
local ok, data, info = pcall(store.GetVersionAtTimeAsync, store, key, updateUnixMs - 1)
-- or browse: store:ListVersionsAsync(key, Enum.SortDirection.Descending, minMs, maxMs, 50)
--          then store:GetVersionAsync(key, versionId)
if ok and data then
    store:UpdateAsync(key, function(old) return data end) -- write as new latest version
end
```
Rules/limits: restore while the player is offline (or kick/lock the session) so the live session doesn't overwrite it; write through UpdateAsync with your session lock/version counter bumped. Pre-update version must still be within 30 days; hourly granularity means writes within the same hour collapse. Version reads count against DataStore budgets; log every restore. Open Cloud DataStore API and the Creator Hub Data Stores Manager offer the same version list/revert outside the game.
D13:
Use Open Cloud with an external backend.
(1) Announcement: the panel calls Open Cloud Messaging (PublishUniverseMessage, cloud/v2 universes/{id}:publishMessage) on topic e.g. "Announce". Every server subscribes once at startup with MessagingService:SubscribeAsync("Announce", ...) and shows the message to its players. Best effort, ~1-2 s, 1 kB message limit.
(2) Grant item: the source of truth is the player's DataStore. Panel writes a pending grant: either a separate "Grants" DataStore/queue entry keyed by UserId via the Open Cloud DataStore entries API, which the game merges into the profile on join (idempotent by grant id), or edit the profile directly only if offline. For online players also publish a "Grant" message with userId + grantId so the server holding that player pulls it immediately; servers apply grants via UpdateAsync and mark them consumed, so offline/online/duplicate deliveries are all safe.
Security: separate minimal-scope API keys (messaging publish; datastore read/create/update restricted to that universe), stored in the backend's secret manager, never in the browser. Panel behind admin auth, audit-log and make grants reversible. Handle 429 with retry-after.
D14:
BindableEvent/BindableFunction arguments are serialized and copied across the call: tables become new tables, metatables are stripped, functions are dropped, non-string mixed keys get converted, and nil holes truncate arrays. Instances (the Player) pass by reference, but invObject arrives as a plain table without its class metatable, so invObject:AddItem() fails (attempt to call nil), and any mutations affect only the copy, not the original state.
ModuleScripts: put the inventory class and a per-player registry in a ModuleScript (e.g. InventoryService). Each server script require()s it and gets the same cached module table (require runs once per environment), so all scripts share live objects with metatables intact and call methods directly (InventoryService.get(player):AddItem(...)). Use module functions/a pure-Luau Signal module for in-process events instead of Bindables. Keep plain data only when crossing real boundaries (remotes, Actors, DataStores) and rebuild objects on arrival. Note server and client get separate module copies; modules aren't a client-server channel. Avoid yielding at module top level.
D15:
UnreliableRemoteEvent is right for high-frequency, cosmetic, superseded-by-the-next-update data: aim/look direction, footstep VFX, cheap visual positions. Losing or reordering one packet doesn't matter because the next one replaces it, and it doesn't clog the reliable queue, so hits and purchases stop being delayed.
Constraints: no delivery or ordering guarantee (include a sequence number/timestamp and drop stale ones). Payloads over ~1,000 bytes are dropped silently, so keep them tiny (e.g. compressed angles or buffers). Same API as RemoteEvent (FireServer/FireAllClients/OnServerEvent). Never use it for state that must arrive: hits, damage, purchases, ability start/stop, inventory. Still validate on server (types, NaN, magnitude, rate limit per player).
Also reduce the load: send 10-20 Hz instead of 30, only when changed, FireAllClients except sender or only to nearby players, and let clients derive footsteps locally from character movement instead of networking them.
D16:
Problems:
- Message size limit is 1 kB; 3 KB payloads fail to publish.
- Throughput: 500 servers x 12 publishes/min = 6,000 messages/min into one topic, each delivered to 500 subscribers (~3M deliveries/min). Per-topic receive limit is 40 + 80 x servers/min (~40k) and experience-wide limits apply (400 + 200 x servers/min); one hot topic gets throttled and messages dropped.
- Per-server sends 600 + 240 x players/min; subscriptions per server 20 + 8 x players.
- Delivery is best-effort, ~1-2 s latency, can be dropped, duplicated or out of order, and no history: a newly started server sees nothing until each server publishes again, and dead servers never send a removal, so the list goes stale.
Fix: use MemoryStoreService SortedMap: each server SetAsync(JobId, smallSummary, 90 s expiry) every 30 s; lobby servers GetRangeAsync (paged) every 15-30 s. Expiry removes dead servers automatically. Keep values small; mind the 1,000 + 120 x CCU request units/min budget. Use MessagingService only for small, rare events.
D17:
Limits: HttpService allows 500 requests per minute per game server (all HttpService traffic combined); over the limit, requests fail/stall (~30 s). Per-join x3 + per-kill calls spike on busy servers. Your analytics backend also receives the sum of every server. Requests can fail for network reasons regardless.
Correct setup:
- Enable HTTP requests in Game Settings (Security; HttpEnabled), server-only.
- Batch: queue events in memory and flush one POST every ~30-60 s (and on BindToClose), with a size cap; drop/aggregate low-value events.
- Wrap RequestAsync/PostAsync in pcall; retry only 429/5xx with exponential backoff and a cap; don't retry 4xx.
- Prefer built-in AnalyticsService for game analytics where possible.
- Never hard-code the Open Cloud API key: anyone with place/edit access or a leaked copy gets it. Store it in the experience's Secrets store (Creator Hub) and use HttpService:GetSecret("name") to get a Secret object, adding it to headers. Use a minimal-scope key, IP/experience restricted, and rotate the leaked one.
D18:
Client camera: Heartbeat runs after physics, out of sync with rendering, and the default camera module also writes at Camera priority, so the CFrame fights and lags a frame -> jitter. Use RunService:BindToRenderStep("Follow", Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value + 1, fn) (runs just before the frame renders, after the default camera; use Camera.Value - 1 or CameraType Scriptable if replacing it). RenderStepped/PreRender also work but BindToRenderStep gives ordering. Use dt for smoothing.
Server projectile: RenderStepped/BindToRenderStep/PreRender are client-only (there's no rendering on the server), hence the error. Use RunService.Heartbeat (alias PostSimulation) to step projectiles and read final physics, or PreSimulation to set state before physics. Step by dt (or time()/GetServerTimeNow), not frame counts, since server Heartbeat drops below ~60 Hz under load. For deterministic server-authority games, RunService:BindToSimulation. Check RunService:IsClient()/IsServer() for shared modules.
D19:
Use the Input Action System (IAS) for a new 2026 game; ContextActionService still works but IAS is the forward path and what Server Authority requires.
Structure (instances, configured in Studio or code): InputContext (a group of actions; Enabled, Priority, Sink; enable/disable whole modes like 'OnFoot' vs 'Menu') -> InputAction (Type: Bool, Direction1D/2D/3D, ViewportPosition; e.g. Sprint Bool, Interact Bool; events Pressed, Released, StateChanged; GetState()) -> InputBinding children (KeyCode e.g. LeftShift / ButtonL3 / a touch UIButton, Primary/SecondaryModifier, Scale). Scripts listen to actions, not devices; bind keyboard, gamepad and touch for each.
Default player scripts: being migrated to IAS via Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem: opt-in since June 2026 (default Disabled), planned default Enabled early 2027, property removal mid-2027. That breaks PlayerModule:GetControls() hacks and forked PlayerModules (forks need StarterPlayer.CreateDefaultPlayerModule = Disabled). Disable movement by disabling an InputContext, not via GetControls.
D20:
Turn on: set Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server (full release July 9, 2026; some docs still say beta). It forces NextGenerationReplication, Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem, SignalBehavior = Deferred, StreamingEnabled and UseFixedSimulation.
What it does: the server is authoritative for simulation of characters and physics; clients run predicted simulation from their inputs and the engine resimulates (rollback) when the server disagrees. Clients can no longer move their character or owned parts arbitrarily, blocking speed/teleport/fling exploits that network ownership allowed.
Script changes:
- Gameplay simulation code goes in RunService:BindToSimulation(fn) inside a ModuleScript required by both server and client so prediction matches.
- Read input via InputAction (IAS), not UserInputService/ContextActionService.
- Use time() for timing, not tick/os.time/os.clock.
- Guard side effects (sounds, VFX, remotes) with RunService:IsResimulating().
- No Destroy, reparent or EquipTool inside bound functions; don't cache AnimationTracks; camera via Player:GetCameraState().
- Replicated state via attributes (first 64, names/strings max 50 chars).
- SetNetworkOwner tricks no longer apply; deferred signals change event timing.
D21:
Fixed-step simulation: Workspace.UseFixedSimulation with RunService:BindToSimulation(fn, frequency, priority) (frequency is Enum.StepFrequency: Hz60, Hz30 (default), Hz15, Hz10, Hz5, Hz1; priority default 2000). Bound functions run at a fixed tick independent of render FPS, with a constant dt, on both client and server, so 30 and 144 FPS players and the server compute the same results. RunService:BindToAnimation has the same signature for animation-side work.
Requirements: UseFixedSimulation enabled (Server Authority mode / AuthorityMode = Server forces it). Put the movement code in a ModuleScript both sides require so client prediction and server match. Use the step's dt/time(), not os.clock/tick; read input through InputActions. Make it resimulation-safe: no side effects or use RunService:IsResimulating() to skip sounds/remotes; no Destroy/reparent inside. Without fixed sim, use a fixed-dt accumulator with a clamp. Caveat: Motor6D Transform writes during fixed sim may not apply (unverified).
D22:
Lighting.Technology has been deprecated (2025-2026) and replaced by two properties: Lighting.LightingStyle (Realistic default, or Soft) and Lighting.PrioritizeLightingQuality (bool, default true). Technology is now locked to RobloxScriptSecurity, so reading/writing it from a LocalScript errors, and it is hidden/deprecated in Studio's Properties. Legacy/Compatibility/Unified options are gone.
Also, lighting technology is an experience-wide visual setting; graphics quality is the player's own (Settings quality level), so a settings menu shouldn't flip it per client anyway.
Fix: drop the Technology write. Set LightingStyle = Enum.LightingStyle.Realistic with PrioritizeLightingQuality = true (closest to Future) in Studio; if offering a client 'quality' toggle, adjust cosmetic properties (shadows, effects, particle counts) instead, and let the engine scale by the user's graphics quality. Note ShadowSoftness only applies with Realistic.
